findings.summary: Module top-level `export const env = loadEnv()` runs at import time; defeats the buildApp(env) DI seam required for the JWT_SECRET fail-fast test (enriched bullet 10).
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the eager singleton: remove line 26 and require every consumer to take Env via constructor/factory args. main.ts calls `const env = loadEnv(process.env)` then passes it into buildApp/createLogger/createDb. Integration tests that need to override JWT_SECRET then call buildApp({ ...baseEnv, JWT_SECRET: 'too-short' }) and observe the throw without a prior import-time crash.

findings.summary: logger.ts imports the eager `env` singleton from env.js, so any module that imports logger triggers loadEnv() at module-load; propagates the eager-load coupling across the entire app.
findings.suggested_fix: Convert logger to a factory: `export function createLogger(level: Env['LOG_LEVEL']): pino.Logger`. main.ts builds it once after `loadEnv`; tests pass any level they like. Move REDACT_PATHS as-is. Update withRequestId to accept the base logger.

findings.summary: UserId is defined as `Brand<string,'UserId'>` here, but packages/contracts/src/auth.ts defines an incompatible Zod-branded UserId; values typed via one cannot flow into the other without casts.
findings.suggested_fix: Pick one source of truth. Either (a) re-export the Zod-branded type from contracts and drop the local Brand-based definition, or (b) define the structural brand once in shared/ids.ts and have contracts' z.string().uuid() return that exact branded type via `.transform(s => s as UserId)`. Same for RefreshTokenId.

findings.summary: csrfCookieOptions sets secure:true unconditionally; browsers will not send the csrf cookie over plain HTTP, breaking the double-submit flow in local dev (Vite proxy on http://localhost) and in integration tests that drive Hono via app.request with http URLs.
findings.suggested_fix: Make `secure` env-gated for all three presets: `secure: env.NODE_ENV !== 'development' && env.NODE_ENV !== 'test'` (or pass secure via factory args so http.ts stays env-free). Keep HttpOnly+SameSite=Lax invariants. Document the production posture in a JSDoc comment.

findings.summary: ErrorCode includes 'INTERNAL' but no InternalError subclass exists; errorHandler middleware (next wave) cannot construct one to surface 5xx with a stable code.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `export class InternalError extends AppError { override readonly code = 'INTERNAL' as const; constructor(message='Internal error', details?){ super('INTERNAL', message, 500, details); this.name='InternalError'; Object.setPrototypeOf(this, new.target.prototype); } }`. Or drop 'INTERNAL' from ErrorCode and have errorHandler render unknown errors with a literal 500 body it composes inline.

findings.summary: Base AppError ctor sets this.name='AppError' but every subclass immediately overwrites it; the base assignment is dead-but-harmless code.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop `this.name = 'AppError'` from the base constructor (line 26) — subclasses already set their own name. Reduces noise. The Object.setPrototypeOf line should stay.

findings.summary: refreshResponse and meResponse are structurally identical to loginResponse — three names for the same shape. Acceptable now, will become noise if any of them diverges.
findings.suggested_fix: Either alias them (`export const refreshResponse = loginResponse`) or keep distinct for future divergence per the task spec. No action required this wave; revisit if/when wave-7 auth.routes introduces fields specific to one response.
